habitat: Area of complex geology with mix of sandstone, gypsum, and limestone forming alternating layers. Tallest mesa capped by sandstone. Greater area dominated by grassland and junipers, although gypsum soils relatively barren and comprised of typical central New Mexico gypsum flora, dominated by Tiquilia hispidissima and Sporobolus nealleyi. Oenothera hartwegii subsp. filifolia, Mentzelia perennis, Acleisanthes lanceolata, and Nama carnosa also present on gypsum. Non-gypsum soils with much greater vegetation cover. Conditions good.
locality: Just N of WSMR P Route 5, a few mi E of Lemitar.
name: Acleisanthes lanceolata var. lanceolata
